To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the three-dimensional structure at a resolution of 1.9 A of NAD+-phenylalanine dehyrogenase from Nocardiasp239 and that the structure of this enzyme has been solved in complex with the substrate analog, alpha-methylphenylalanine.
we have crystallized NADH-dependent phenylalanine-dehydrogenase from the bacterium Nocardia sp.239 and that this is a new member of the family of octameric amino-acid dehydragenases.
The NAD+-dependent, phenylalanine-degrading phenylalanine (Phe) dehydrogenase (PheDH) from Nocardia has been crystallized in the presence and in the absence of its substrates and coenzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new biocatalytic process for the synthesis of chiral amines.
the development of a novel enzyme-based method for the synthesis of chiral amino acids.
the development of novel biocatalytic processes for the manufacture of fine chemicals, and the elucidation of the molecular basis for their catalytic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this enzyme has been crystallized, that the crystal form obtained is suitable for the determination of the three- dimensional structure of the protein and that the structure of the protein has been determined.
this enzyme is the first example of a PheDH which is not a member of the octameric family.
this is the first report of the crystal structure of an NAD+-dependent amino-acid dehydrgenase from a Gram-positive actinomycete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this enzyme is an excellent candidate for the determination of its three-dimensional structure.

we have obtained the first crystal structures of an amino-acd dehydrogenase with the potential to be used for the chiral production of high-value amino-acids and for the diagnosis of a serious genetic disease.
we have crystallized a phenylalanine-dehydrogenase enzyme which has been shown to be related to the wider family of amino acid dehydrogenase superfamily.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallization of NAD-dependent PheDH was successfully achieved by using ammonium sulfate and the enzyme substrates as precipitants.
the crystallization of NAD-dependent phenylalanine from Nocardia species can be done in the absence or presence of its co-substrates, NADH and phenylalanine, or phenylpyruvate.
the crystallization of NAD-dependent phenylalanine from Nocardia 239 is possible, but it is difficult.
